name: Drab Green
lede: Drab Green is a grey-leaning leaf green, a survey name for a green that has lost its brightness.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd survey of 2010, and our sources record nothing earlier under these words [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[moss]], about 5 units away [1].

The closest old term in the books is olive drab. St Clair's glossary defines it as green with plenty of gray and brown, a dull olive [2]. That entry describes a family of dull, grayed greens, but this swatch is a survey name for a screen color, not a pigment [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive a color near this swatch appears in 84 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.35 per cent, which is rarer than 55 per cent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s at 3.9 times the expected rate, and it is most over-represented in France, at 2.4 times [3]. These are photographs of aged paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
